title: Post-Lie nonexistence with a semisimple target
description: A unimodular-source obstruction for finite-dimensional complex post-Lie algebras, proving nonexistence for perfect nonsemisimple sources and semisimple targets.
abstract: Let g be a finite-dimensional complex unimodular Lie algebra and n a complex semisimple Lie algebra of the same dimension. We prove that if two Lie algebra homomorphisms j₁, j₂ : g → n have invertible difference, then g is semisimple. The integrated left-right action has a holomorphic infinitesimal determinant. Unimodularity makes this determinant invariant, and its constancy on an open orbit extends to the whole target group. Transitivity and simple connectedness then identify the source and target manifolds; their compact-form homology rules out a nonzero source radical. Consequently a perfect nonsemisimple complex source and a semisimple target admit no post-Lie algebra structure.
plain_language: A Lie algebra describes infinitesimal symmetries. A post-Lie product is an extra operation that makes two Lie brackets on the same vector space compatible. This paper asks when that compatibility is impossible.

The result rules out every finite-dimensional complex pair whose source is perfect but not semisimple and whose target is semisimple. In this language, perfect means generated by its brackets, while semisimple means having no nonzero solvable ideal. The paper actually proves a stronger obstruction using the weaker source condition called unimodularity.

The striking step is geometric: a local compatibility condition would force two associated symmetry spaces to be the same manifold. Their topology then detects the source’s solvable part and shows that it must vanish. This turns a problem about algebraic identities into a short obstruction from geometry and homology.

The argument addresses the semisimple-target conjecture described by Burde and Dekimpe, extending earlier special cases. It adapts a determinant method with an explicit predecessor in Baues’s work and uses established Lie theory; historical first priority is not claimed.
result: Theorem 1: let g and n be complex Lie algebras of the same finite dimension. If tr(ad_g x) = 0 for every x ∈ g, n is semisimple, and homomorphisms j₁, j₂ : g → n have an invertible linear difference, then g is semisimple.

Corollary 3: if a post-Lie structure exists on (g, n), with g unimodular and n semisimple, then g must be semisimple. Every perfect Lie algebra is unimodular, so a perfect nonsemisimple source admits no such structure with any semisimple target.

The homomorphisms need not be injective, algebraic, or have closed integrated images. Their invertible difference is the transversality assumption. The zero-dimensional case is included, with the zero algebra semisimple by convention.
The result supplies the semisimple-target conclusion conjectured on printed p. 2689 of Oberwolfach Report 46/2023. The separate conjectures there concerning nilpotent targets are outside this result.
limitations: The published theorem is stated for finite-dimensional complex Lie algebras. It does not provide a separate treatment of arbitrary real forms, positive characteristic or infinite dimension.
Unimodularity cannot simply be omitted. Remark 4 supplies a three-dimensional nonunimodular solvable source with two homomorphisms into sl₂(C) whose difference is invertible.

A merely reductive target is not covered. Central directions change both the inner-derivation reduction and the topological obstruction; earlier literature contains perfect-source examples with reductive nonsemisimple targets.

The orbit map identifies manifolds, and is not asserted to be a group homomorphism. The proof’s conclusion is semisimplicity of the source; a Lie algebra isomorphism is not inferred solely from that manifold identification.

The determinant method, transverse-pair formulation and Lie-theoretic and topological inputs have substantial predecessors. The literature comparison is bounded, and the original body of Onishchik’s 1969 decomposition paper was not accessible in this review. No exhaustive novelty or first-priority certificate is given.

Exact finite diagnostic checks accompany the paper. They cannot establish the global integration, transitivity, covering-space or homology arguments, which depend on the analytical proof and its cited classical results.

why_it_works: Integrate the two homomorphisms to simply connected complex groups. Their left-right action has a globally holomorphic determinant measuring whether its infinitesimal orbit directions span the target tangent space.

Unimodularity makes this determinant invariant. It is a nonzero constant on an open orbit, so the holomorphic identity theorem makes it that same constant everywhere. All orbits are open, forcing transitivity on the connected target.
The stabilizer is closed and discrete. The orbit map is therefore a covering, and simple connectedness makes it a diffeomorphism of the source and target manifolds.

A simply connected solvable radical is contractible. The source retracts onto the compact form of its semisimple Levi factor, while the target has a nonzero homology class in the degree of its full complex dimension. A nonzero source radical would make those homology groups incompatible.
For a semisimple post-Lie target, inner derivations yield the established pair j₁ = R + I and j₂ = R. Their difference is the identity, so the obstruction applies.
collaboration: I welcome substantive collaboration on independent verification of the global-action and homology argument, its relationship to the classical decomposition literature, and preparation for journal review. Expertise in post-Lie algebras, Lie-group actions or complex Lie theory would be particularly useful.
followup_rationale: No follow-up is proposed. Nearby nilpotent-target conjectures are pre-existing questions, and simply changing the field, target class or unimodularity condition supplies neither a new conjecture nor a sufficiently developed research mechanism. The review does not meet the high bar for adding a separate public research direction.
